findings.claim: When `repair_loop` already returned `EXHAUSTED` because `_repair()`'s own `_over_budget()` check (line 1552-1553) fired — i.e. the budget ceiling was hit with zero additional spend between that check and this one — the notes-eligibility check at line 1617 calls `_over_budget()` again with the identical `spent`/`spec.budget_usd` pair. `_over_budget()` (lines 1306-1321) is not idempotent: every call where it returns True also `emit()`s a `Budget` event. The result is two byte-identical `Budget` events recorded for a single real budget breach, back-to-back with no intervening turn, which is new: before this diff execution went straight from `repair_loop`'s `EXHAUSTED` return to constructing `CellOutcome` with no further budget check in between. Anyone reading the task's event/watch log (the mechanism the code's own comments say is how an operator tells EXHAUSTED-by-no-progress apart from EXHAUSTED-by-budget) now sees the ceiling reported as hit twice for what was one occurrence.

`render_pr_body` is called here with every other outcome field (`reviews`, `rebut_result`, `advisory_gates`, ...) but never `notes=outcome.notes`, so the notes extracted, hashed and written to `notes.json` by `_drive_cell` never reach the packaged PR body in production — the default `notes=""` on `render_pr_body` silently swallows them. Every acceptance criterion and every test exercises `render_pr_body` directly with an explicit `notes=` argument or `CellOutcome`/`session.py` in isolation, so no gate or test touches this call site, and the one channel this spec exists to build is wired everywhere except the one place that actually produces a pull request.

`notes_worth_asking = bool(spec.forbidden) or bool(policy.protected)` is asserted by the docstring/comment to fire on *either* a declared `forbidden` list or a repo-wide `protected` one, but every test that exercises the notes turn (`test_the_notes_artifact_is_hashed_when_it_is_produced`, `test_the_notes_turn_is_skipped_once_the_task_is_over_budget`, and the skip test) sets `spec.forbidden` non-empty; none constructs a spec with an empty `forbidden` against a policy declaring `protected` paths to prove the `or bool(policy.protected)` half does anything. Deleting that clause so the line reads `notes_worth_asking = bool(spec.forbidden)` leaves all three notes-related tests green, silently disabling the channel for exactly the protected-path scenario item 75 was about.

No test drives an `AgentFailed` through the new notes turn (every other agent call in this module — plan, repair, rebuttal — has at least one such test), so the `except implement.AgentFailed` branch that calls `_failed_turn` and checkpoints a phase-start message is asserted by nothing; removing the try/except entirely (letting the exception propagate) would not fail any existing test.
